proposals.evidence: CDIAL 7136 nikaṭam explicitly gives Bshk. nīer and northwestern neṛe/neḍi/neḍḍhi “near”. The survey nīar/niḍe forms fit; initial m in mere remains a different comparison. Reviewed comparison: bundeli_atarra nerɛ “near” (f_liqggsmbw27ti). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

Reviewed comparison: dhundari_bamore kūṇa “who?” (f_7vq2ppmofwnwy). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10066 mārayati gives the mār- kill verb; maral/marla and māryo are ordinary eastern -l and western -y past/infinitive formations. Mār-diyo contains a give light verb and is not assigned as a simple inherited stem. Reviewed comparison: bundeli_atarra mara “he killed” (f_lc3dx7rp6qkna). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6507.2 *dekṣati gives the dekh- see verb and regional v-/d- variation through transmission. Dekh-ta, dekh-u and ordinary -y past forms retain that stem; dekh-liyo requires the take light verb to be analyzed. Reviewed comparison: Dang dekʰnu “he sees; he saw” (f_cxv7xeg25h72u). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
